$Comment: Roaming Temple rig. Offsets are model units (one prefab block) in titan-local space: +X right, +Y up, -Z forward. The root sits on the ground, so Pelvis's offset is the hip height, which here is the whole length of a leg.

A quadruped, so none of the player-rig bone names apply and none are here. There is no ClipSet either: nothing about a temple should sway or breathe, and with the body pinned to its bind pose the only thing that moves is the legs, which the foot planner drives from the body's own velocity. A missing clip set resolves to the bind pose rather than an error, so this is a supported way to build one rather than an omission.

The leg is authored as a single 25-block pillar and cut into three by SliceMinY/SliceMaxY, which is what gives it a knee without anyone having to save the prefab out three times. It tapers the other way up from a limb: 8x8 at the foot narrowing to 2x2 where it meets the body, so the wide end is the one on the ground. The cuts are at the two places the cross-section steps in.

The leg is 25 long but the hip only sits 23 up, and the two numbers are deliberately different. The IK drives the last bone's origin onto the ground, so a chain whose reach exactly equalled the hip height would stand dead straight on flat ground with nothing left to bend, and would simply fail to reach the moment a foot had to step down. The two spare blocks are the knee's working room.

Foot pivot is 0, not the bottom of its slice, which puts the bone's origin on the sole rather than at the ankle. That is the point the IK is actually aiming at and the point the sole is levelled about, so the foot plants on the ground instead of hanging its own height below the spot the solver picked.

Every bone with geometry is Hollow. The body is 7592 blocks and two thirds of them are buried in the middle of it where nothing will ever see them; at one entity per block that filling is the difference between a titan this size being possible and not.

WeakpointSockets are twelve per leg, on all four faces of the calf and thigh. Six are rolled at spawn from the whole pool of forty-eight, so which legs are worth attacking is different every time, and a leg can come up bare. Offsets are measured from each bone's own pivot, which sits at the joint it hangs from rather than inside the shape, so every socket states its Normal explicitly: derived from the offset they would all point at the floor. Calf faces sit at 3.5 out and thigh faces at 2.5, which is the surface of each slice, and the normals tilt up a little so the crystals grow at an angle out of the rock rather than jutting out level like shelves.

Bones.$Comment: The hub the island and all four legs hang off. Carries no geometry: the body slab is a child so that the pivot the legs are measured from is the underside rim, not the middle of the rock.
Bones.Name: Pelvis

Bones.$Comment: The island. Authored 33x25x34 with a keel that hangs lowest down the middle and a rim at about y8 where the legs meet it, so the pivot is that rim height and the keel is left clearing the ground by a good sixteen blocks. Climbable on every exposed face rather than only the top: the top is a temple with walls and stairs, and a player who can stand on the roof but walks through the pillars is worse than one who cannot get up at all.
Bones.Name: Body_Mesh

Bones.$Comment: Front left leg. Anchored 11 out on both axes: far enough for a wide mausoleum stance while the island still overhangs its own legs, and about as far as they go before the narrow top of the leg stops meeting solid keel. Legs are climbable too, mostly so they are solid to walk into rather than because anyone is meant to get up one.
Bones.Name: FL-Thigh

Bones.$Comment: Dropped 15 rather than 10 so the origin lands under the sole instead of at the ankle. That makes the shin-to-foot segment 15 long against the thigh's 10, giving the chain the 25 of reach the leg is actually built out of, and leaves the foot's own 5 blocks stacked above the point the solver plants.
Bones.Name: FL-Foot

$Comment: RestOffset is measured from Pelvis in the same axes as a bone Offset, so X and Z just repeat the leg's own anchor and the foot rests directly under the hip it belongs to. Y is the drop back down to the ground, and only seeds the search: the planner snaps the result to whatever the terrain actually is. GaitPhase pairs the legs diagonally: the planner rounds it to one of two groups and only lets one group be off the ground at a time, so front-left swings with back-right and the thing is always standing on the other two. Stride is short for the size of it on purpose, because a slow walk with long strides reads as gliding.

PoleDirection is the way the knee bends, in titan-local space, and each leg points diagonally away from the middle rather than all four pointing forward. That is what stops the thing having a front: a temple that walks off sideways looks the same as one walking towards you, and the legs splay out under the island like a table's rather than folding the way a runner's do. Each is the leg's own anchor direction normalised, so the knee bends along the same diagonal the leg already sits on.
IkChains.Name: Leg_FL
